title: Florida property-manager identity review
hypothesis: An active Florida broker record can support a property-management identity candidate only when the management signal belongs to an independently operating broker. It cannot establish ownership of the management business, ownership of a phone, or permission to use a residence or private-phone lookup.
ownerSource: The implemented FL DBPR real-estate adapter exposes active BK Broker rows. Its current property-management filter uses employer text only, so it identifies an employed broker candidate rather than an owner-confirming property-manager source.
phoneSource: The Florida register contains no phone field. The current recipe-B route carries a licensee street into parcel/skip-trace processing; that residential/private-contact path is outside this review's permitted scope and must remain held.

workflow.label: Active Florida broker record
workflow.detail: Read a Current, Active, Florida BK Broker record from the public DBPR extract; it supplies identity facts, not a phone.

workflow.label: Property-management business signal?
workflow.detail: Assess management vocabulary on the broker's DBA or employer. Employer-only evidence can describe a worker rather than an owner candidate.

workflow.label: Hold generic real-estate broker
workflow.detail: Do not relabel a generic broker as a property manager without a property-management, rental, leasing, or management business signal.

workflow.label: Independent operating signal?
workflow.detail: A sole broker with a matching DBA is a stronger identity candidate. An employer-backed broker remains employee/role evidence until independently corroborated.

workflow.label: Hold employee or unresolved role
workflow.detail: Do not call an employed broker the owner of the employer's property-management business.

workflow.label: Published business contact available?
workflow.detail: Use only a separately lawful, explicitly published business contact in a future approved route; do not derive a person contact from the licensee address.

workflow.label: Hold residential or private-contact path
workflow.detail: The register has no phone. Do not send its residential-style address to parcel, skip trace, phone append, or property search for this industry review.

workflow.label: Business-contact and compliance gates
workflow.detail: A future approved published-business-contact route must record line type, reachability, DNC/TCPA, suppression, freshness, and independent owner evidence separately.

workflow.label: Hold failed contact or owner evidence
workflow.detail: Keep office, non-mobile, unreachable, suppressed, or candidate-only cases out of owner-confirmed delivery.

workflow.label: Deliver supported classification
workflow.detail: Only recorded, independent current ownership and handset evidence plus all contact gates can support an owner-confirmed classification.

edges.label: only register address or private lookup path
all owner and contact gates pass

failures.risk: The live filter selects an employer-backed broker at a property-management firm while missing a sole broker whose DBA identifies property management.
failures.mitigation: In flReRecord, calculate the management signal from DBA and employer, but emit a property-manager filter value only for a sole broker with the matching DBA; hold employer-backed rows as unresolved role evidence.

failures.risk: The adapter reads only regions 1 through 7 although the verified catalog identifies FL DBPR regional files 1 through 14.
failures.mitigation: Expand FL_RE_FILES to all fourteen documented regions and retain the same positional parser and active-BK gates; add fixture coverage for a later-region request.

failures.risk: A broker license, DBA, or property-management employer is described as proof that a named person owns the management company.
failures.mitigation: Preserve all qualifying people as identity candidates until separate current ownership evidence is recorded.

failures.risk: The recipe-B runner uses the broker street to reach parcel and skip-trace processing despite no register phone field.
failures.mitigation: For property_manager, hold this residential/private-contact path. Do not use parcel, property search, skip trace, or phone append as a correction for this workflow.

failures.risk: A property manager is sourced from prohibited DMV, South Carolina, or Utah license-list routes.
failures.mitigation: Use none of those sources; the reviewed source is Florida DBPR real estate only and any future source needs an explicit legal/source review.

iterations.hypothesis: The live Florida property-manager route selects independently operating property-management brokers from the broker file.
iterations.test: Five-case synthetic code audit on 2026-09-24 using flReRecord, splitRegisterSource, registerSourceFor, and route; no network, phone, address lookup, paid call, secret, or personal contact data. Cases: active BK broker with property-management employer; sole BK broker with property-management DBA; rental employer; leasing employer; generic sole broker.
iterations.observed: The route maps Florida property management to recipe B and fl_re:property_management. The employer, rental, and leasing cases were marked Broker: Property Management and selected; the sole broker with a property-management DBA and the generic sole broker were both marked Broker and not selected. This confirms the filter follows employer text, not the advertised DBA/business-name rule, and admits an employment role. The adapter request stops after region 7. This audit measures parser/routing behavior only, not business coverage, ownership, phone outcome, reachability, DNC, or delivery.
iterations.change: Treat the route as partial. Make the property-management marker dependent on a sole broker's matching DBA, retain employer-backed brokers as unresolved, and expand the adapter from seven to fourteen catalogued regions before any future source-coverage measurement. Keep all residential/private-contact processing held.

measurement.result: Five synthetic parser/routing cases: property-management employer selected; property-management DBA on a sole broker not selected; rental employer selected; leasing employer selected; generic sole broker not selected. flRe requests regions 1-7 only. Code audit only: no live rows, phone values, addresses, ownership checks, reachability, DNC, or delivery measurements.

cost.basis: Offline fixture/code audit only; no paid discovery, private lookup, append, or phone verification was invoked.
cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. The historical property_manager Anas figures use a different denominator and are not a per-clean cost for this workflow.

implementation.summary: The brain routes Florida property managers through a real-estate broker adapter and a business_type filter. The parser has current/active/BK guards but derives the management marker only from employer text, then recipe B sends selected identity rows toward address-based tracing. No property-manager-specific published-business-contact or owner-confirming adapter is implemented; the residential/private-contact branch is outside the permitted workflow scope.

nextMeasurement: After the parser correction, run the same five synthetic rows plus a region-8 request fixture: only a sole broker with matching property-management/rental/leasing DBA should enter the candidate branch; employer-backed, generic, inactive, and non-Florida rows should hold. Before any contact experiment, obtain explicit approval for a lawful published-business-contact source and measure business fit, current ownership, line type, DNC/TCPA, reachability, and delivery under separate denominators without residential/private-phone enrichment.
